## Triage: first grade, `enhancement` · `priority:p3` · `domain:spec`, into `pm:queue`. `@objectstack/verify`'s `flows.run` gains a system-principal arm, symmetric with `hooks.run`'s `{ system: true }`

Triage seat (objectstack-wide, seat post #6015) · `session_01AavokzJ5DndAwitDXvKy4U` · 2026-10-13T14:18Z. ⛔ Not a claim, ⛔ not a dispatch.

- **Why p3:** HotCRM carries an interim helper (`runScheduledFlow`, objectstack-ai/hotcrm#2091) and nothing is blocked. The runtime's refusal of a member start (#22310, #22407) is correct and stays.
- **Queue rule:** a named published surface (`@objectstack/verify`) and a named consumer (HotCRM's scheduled-flow suites).
- **Lane:** a new arm on a published kit's API widens its public surface, so `Clause-②: yes`, spec-lane work with contract-tier review, whichever seat found it.
- **Direction:**
  - `flows.run` (or a sibling) takes a system-principal arm. It starts the flow the way the schedule or trigger tick does, through the in-process automation service, as `hooks.run`'s `{ system: true }` (`b4ce5e2`) does for hooks.
  - ⛔ No HTTP door starts a flow as the system principal. `POST /automation/:name/trigger` keeps refusing a member start with 403.
  - **Pins:** a self-triggered elevated flow starts through the new arm; the same call `as` a member still answers 403 `PERMISSION_DENIED`.
- **After it ships:** HotCRM retires its helper, as its comment says.
- Triage: lands in `packages/verify` (`domain:spec`, Clause-② yes); rationale: an app tests its own scheduled flow end to end through the kit.

Container & model: `M`, `mode:subagent`, `model: default (no path-derived mandate; floor · default · ceiling); Clause-② yes ⇒ CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER review before the queue`
Clause-②: yes

Thread-read: 6147649246
Serial constraints cleared: no open PR touches `packages/verify/**` (read at this act across every open PR's file list).

Read on `origin/main` `5fd2c76d6` at 2026-10-14T20:52Z: `flows.run(name, params, opts: AsUser)` (`handle.ts:371`) dispatches through the runtime's `HttpDispatcher` with the caller's bearer only; `hooks.run` takes `{ system: true }`.

## Review: ACCEPT · PR #23551 @ `ba08362c27a52033c9472ccf01769b0afc74bea8` · `domain:spec` seat 3 · 2026-10-14T22:38Z

Session `session_01D6F9axfoPzR7t8G1J7Ytzz` · `baozhoutao`. Reviewer of record; checked against GitHub, not the report.

- **Shape:** draft, `Fixes #23255`, `Clause-②: yes`; +400/−6, 4 files, all in `packages/verify`; not governed. Contract-tier review on the PR: **PASS** on this head.
- **The arm:** `flows.run(name, params, { system: true })` calls the booted automation service's `execute`, the trigger's own callback, in process. No runtime file, HTTP door or admission rule changed; the `{ as }` overload still answers 403 `PERMISSION_DENIED` (pinned 6 ways). The returned `FlowRun` goes back into `flows.resume` (pinned on a paused `screen` flow).
- **Failure dialect:** the system arm resolves with the engine's `success: false` result, as a trigger receives it; the TSDoc, README and changeset all say to assert `success` first. A single dialect across both arms is a possible follow-up on the runtime surface; not this card's.
- **Changeset:** `@objectstack/verify` `minor`, additive.
- **After it ships:** HotCRM retires its `runScheduledFlow` helper (objectstack-ai/hotcrm#2091) with one `expect(run.success)` assertion.
- **CI on the head:** in progress at this act; the seat lands on green.
